newsitem.title: UK: Guinness/GrandMet say weren't eyeing Allied Domecq.
newsitem.headline: Guinness/GrandMet say weren't eyeing Allied Domecq.

text.p: Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc said on Monday that neither had had any intention of taking over rival drinks group Allied Domecq before their 20 billion stg merger was decided.

Asked at a press briefing if they had torn up plans to take over Allied Domecq, joint chairman George Bull said there had never been any such intention on the part of either of the British-based food and drinks companies.
"Our wastepaper baskets are empty because neither of us had to tear up any such plans," Bull said.
Analysts said the Guinness merger with GrandMet greatly weakened the position of drinks and retail group Allied Domecq, which is due to report its half year results on Tuesday.
"It presents a tremendously difficult problem for Allied," said Philip Hawkins, analyst at Merrill Lynch.
"They will have to look for strategic partners, otherwise they will continue to see their market share erode further and continue to underperform," he said.
The most Allied can hope for is to sew up a deal with Seagram Co or fall to a predator such as American Brands or Brown-Forman Corp, analysts said.
